CRUSH INJURY 
 
 
Causes 
* Extensive soft tissue trauma 
- Community assault 
- Sjambok injury 
* Snake bite 
* Compartment syndrome 
* Strenuous exercise 
* Hyperthermia 
* Electric injury  
* Burns (3rd & 4th degree) 
* Severe sepsis  
* Metabolic myopathies 
* Drug overdose 
- Isoniazid 
- Corticosteroids 
- Colchicine 
- Anti-malarial 
- Heroine 
- Zidovudine 
 
Clinical Examination 
* Tramline bruising 
* Tense, oedematous, painful muscle groups 
* Dark / tea-coloured urine 
* Circulatory shock 
Investigations 
* Blood gas – metabolic acidosis, Ý lactate 
* U-dipstix – haemoglobin / protein  
* eFAST 
* Bloods: Creatinine kinase, myoglobin, U&E, CMP 
ED Management 
 
* ABCD approach to resuscitation 
 
* Aggressive fluid administration 
 
- Crystalloids (Balsol / Ringers Lactate) 
 
- Rate: 15 – 30 ml/kg/hr 
 
* Monitor urinary output 
  - Aim for urinary output of 200 – 300 mls/hr 
 
* Correct Electrolyte Abnormalities 
 
* Indication for Mannitol   
- urine output < 20mls/hr 
 
* Indications for NaHCO3 8.5% (1ml/kg) 
- severe metabolic acidosis  
- hyperkalaemia correction 
 
* Indications for referral for dialysis 
 
- persistent acidosis 
 
- refractory hyperkalaemia 
 
- ß urine output 
 
* Disposition 
 
- Refer Trauma/Surgery depending on cause   
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
